source_text: Vides igitur frustra te peccatum vocasse, si in his operibus, quae Deus fecit, velamen fateamur adhibendum, quod Dominus noster et hominis formator instituit, et homo factus exercuit. Det sane veniam reverentia Redemptoris, quia ad asserendam veritatem mysterii, Manichaeorumque flagitia destruenda, loquimur de carne eius audacter; quod nisi fides exigeret, reverentia modesta non tangeret.
pass_a_gloss: You see therefore that you have called it sin in vain, if in these works which God made we confess a veil must be applied, which our Lord both as former of the human instituted and as a human being made exercised. Let the reverence of the Redeemer indeed grant pardon, because for asserting the truth of the mystery and destroying the outrages of the Manichaeans we speak boldly about his flesh; which unless faith demanded, modest reverence would not touch.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: You therefore see that you vainly called it a sin to acknowledge that a covering must be applied to these works God made: our Lord instituted this as humanity’s maker and practiced it when he became human. May reverence for the Redeemer grant pardon because, to defend the truth of the mystery and destroy the Manichaeans’ wickedness, I speak boldly of his flesh. Unless faith demanded it, restrained reverence would not touch this subject.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
